Created CLAUDE.md for whatsapp-livetranslate-2.0 repository. Key architecture points documented:
- Command framework using interface pattern (Command interface with Execute + Metadata)
- Commands organized by category in internal/handlers/ (admin, fun, translation, utility)
- Service injection via Context.Handler interface
- Owner-only commands use middleware wrapping pattern
- Translation commands auto-registered for all supported languages
- Special handling for sed command (s/) and language code fallback
- Uses whatsmeow for WhatsApp integration, Gemini for AI features
- Environment variable: GEMINI_API_KEY (not GEMINI_KEY)

Transcription feature architecture design for WhatsApp bot:
- Use REST API at localhost:8009 (/api/transcribe/whisper-ivrit for Hebrew)
- Download audio via whatsmeow client.Download(), upload to transcribe container
- Per-chat enable/disable using SQLite table (transcription_settings)
- Commands: /tenable, /tdisable  
- Auto-transcribe in handleMessage() before command routing
- Default language: Hebrew (he), use existing LangDetector for smart detection
- Components: TranscriptionService (HTTP client), TranscriptionStateManager (SQLite), modified event handler
- Error handling: silent fail if service down, user-friendly messages for other errors

Created comprehensive audio transcription implementation plan for WhatsApp bot at docs/plans/2025-01-18-audio-transcription.md. Plan includes:
- 13 tasks across 8 phases following TDD (RED-GREEN-REFACTOR)
- Phase 1: Database schema and state management (SQLite)
- Phase 2: HTTP client for transcription service
- Phase 3: Audio download integration with whatsmeow
- Phase 4: /tenable and /tdisable commands
- Phase 5: Event handler integration (audio processing before command routing)
- Phase 6: Configuration and documentation
- Phase 7: Integration testing
- Phase 8: Final build and deployment
Each task has exact file paths, complete code, test-first approach, and commit messages. No breaking changes to existing functionality.

Dependency analysis completed for audio transcription feature:

**No new dependencies needed!** Current bot already has:
- whatsmeow (has client.Download() for audio)
- go-sqlite3 (for state management)
- godotenv (for config)

**Proven patterns from reference repos:**
1. Audio download: client.Download(audioMessage) returns []byte directly
2. PTT detection: msg.GetAudioMessage().GetPTT() checks for voice notes
3. Temp files: os.CreateTemp("", "whatsapp_audio_*.ogg")
4. Database: Use existing container.DB from sqlstore.New()
5. State schema: Simple chat_jid + enabled boolean
6. Error handling: Silent fail for service unavailable (log only)

**Plan updates needed:**
- Remove ClientInterface.DownloadAudio (use client.Download directly)
- Pass container.DB to StateManager instead of creating new connection
- Add PTT check for voice message detection
- Simplify integration (no new deps)

Updated audio transcription implementation plan with proven patterns from reference repositories:

**Key Updates:**
1. NO new dependencies needed - uses existing whatsmeow, go-sqlite3, godotenv
2. Audio download: Use client.Download(audioMsg) directly (returns []byte)
3. Database: Use container.DB from sqlstore.New() (already initialized in main.go)
4. PTT detection: Added isPTTVoiceNote() helper to distinguish voice notes from audio files
5. Temp files: Use os.CreateTemp("", "whatsapp_audio_*.ogg") pattern
6. Error handling: Silent fail for service unavailable (log only, don't spam user)
7. Simplified Phase 3: Removed ClientInterface.DownloadAudio (use client.Download directly)

**Removed Complexity:**
- No new database connection (reuse container.DB)
- No wrapper methods for audio download
- No additional middleware layers

**Added from Reference Repos:**
- PTT (Push-To-Talk) detection for voice messages
- Proven temp file handling pattern
- Silent error handling for transcription service failures

Plan saved to: docs/plans/2025-01-18-audio-transcription.md

Final implementation plan updated with VibeGram transcription service details:

**VibeGram Service (v5.0) Key Facts:**
- Modular FastAPI app with 17 modules
- Port 8009 (configurable)
- Models: ivrit-ct2 (Hebrew), whisper-v3-turbo (multilingual), deepgram (cloud)
- REST API: POST /api/transcribe/whisper-ivrit with multipart file upload
- Features: diarization, deduplication, summarization, audio caching (SHA256)
- Handles all audio processing internally (FFmpeg, chunking, model loading)

**Integration Strategy:**
- Use REST API (not WebSocket) for simplicity
- Bot downloads audio from WhatsApp (client.Download)
- Upload OGG file to VibeGram via multipart/form-data
- VibeGram returns JSON with transcription text
- Bot sends text back to WhatsApp

**Why This Works:**
- VibeGram already handles complex audio processing
- Bot only needs to bridge WhatsApp ↔ VibeGram
- Clean separation of concerns
- VibeGram's caching reduces duplicate work

Plan location: docs/plans/2025-01-18-audio-transcription.md

WhatsApp LiveTranslate Bot - Video Transcription Feature Analysis

KEY FINDINGS:
1. Current transcription only supports audio via /tenable command
2. Transcription uses Deepgram container at localhost:8009 (configurable via TRANSCRIBE_SERVICE_URL)
3. Service has /api/upload endpoint and multiple transcription endpoints
4. Current flow: Download → Save to temp file → Upload to service → Get file_id → POST to /api/transcribe/* with file path

ARCHITECTURE PATTERNS:
- Command framework: Commands implement Execute() and Metadata()
- Owner-only commands wrapped with RequireOwner() middleware
- WhatsApp message download: client.Download(msg) returns []byte
- Video messages: msg.GetVideoMessage() similar to audio
- Download command uses yt-dlp for URL processing (supports YouTube, Instagram, Twitter, etc.)

TRANSCRIPTION SERVICE API:
- POST /api/upload - Upload file, returns {file_id, filename, size_mb}
- POST /api/transcribe/whisper - For non-Hebrew (whisper-v3-turbo model)
- POST /api/transcribe/whisper-ivrit - For Hebrew (ivrit-ct2 model)  
- POST /api/transcribe/deepgram - For Deepgram model
- Request body: {url: "/app/uploads/file_id", language: "he"}

NEEDED FOR VIDEO TRANSCRIPTION:
1. Extend shouldTranscribe() to check for video messages when /tenable
2. Add handleVideoTranscription() similar to handleAudioTranscription()
3. Add /transcribe command for URL-based transcription (any chat)
4. Extract audio from video before uploading to transcription service OR send video directly if service supports it
5. Support both direct video messages and URLs via yt-dlp download

Deepgram Container Full Capabilities - Video Transcription

CRITICAL DISCOVERY:
The Deepgram container ALREADY handles video transcription end-to-end!

REST API ENDPOINTS:
1. POST /api/upload - Upload file, returns {file_id, filename, size_mb}
2. POST /api/transcribe/whisper-ivrit - Hebrew transcription
3. POST /api/transcribe/whisper - Standard Whisper
4. POST /api/transcribe/deepgram - Deepgram transcription

Each transcription endpoint accepts TWO input methods:
A) multipart/form-data with 'file' field (uploaded file)
B) JSON body with 'url' field: {url: "https://...", language: "he", ...}

AUTOMATIC VIDEO HANDLING:
- download_with_fallback() function tries: yt-dlp first, then ffmpeg
- ffmpeg command includes '-vn' flag = extracts audio from video automatically
- Supports YouTube, Instagram, Twitter, TikTok, etc. via yt-dlp
- Returns final transcription text after complete workflow

BOT IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY:
1. Video Messages: Download from WhatsApp → Upload to /api/upload → POST to /api/transcribe/* with file path
2. URL Transcription: Pass URL directly in JSON body → Deepgram handles download, audio extraction, transcription

NO REDUNDANCY: Bot should NOT use yt-dlp or ffmpeg - Deepgram container already has this!

Language Detection Strategy for Video Transcription

USER REQUIREMENTS:
1. Detect language of video audio
2. Hebrew → use ivrit-ct2 model
3. Non-Hebrew → use Deepgram model
4. Use WebSocket endpoints (already working in /tenable)

BOT'S LANGUAGE DETECTION:
- Has LangDetectService using Lingua library (lingua-go)
- Detects language from TEXT, not audio
- Method: DetectLanguage(text string) (lingua.Language, bool)

DEEPGRAM WEBSOCKET ENDPOINT:
- ws://localhost:8009/ws/transcribe
- Input: {url: "...", model: "ivrit-ct2"|"whisper-v3-turbo"|"deepgram", language: "he"}
- Output: Real-time status updates and transcription chunks
- Returns detected_language in completion message

OPTIMAL STRATEGY:
1. Start WebSocket transcription with whisper-v3-turbo (fast, multilingual)
2. Wait for first transcription chunk
3. Use Lingua to detect language from first chunk text
4. If Hebrew detected:
   - Restart WebSocket with ivrit-ct2 model for better Hebrew quality
5. If non-Hebrew:
   - Restart WebSocket with deepgram model for better quality
6. Continue streaming transcription to completion

ALTERNATIVE (simpler but slower):
1. Transcribe full video with whisper-v3-turbo
2. Detect language from full transcription
3. If mismatch with optimal model, re-transcribe with correct model

WebSocket Implementation Strategy for /transcribe Command

KEY FINDINGS:
1. Bot has gorilla/websocket library in go.mod
2. Bot does NOT currently use WebSockets with Deepgram (uses REST API)
3. LangDetectService (Lingua) detects language from TEXT only, not audio
4. Deepgram WebSocket returns detected_language in response

OPTIMAL IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY:
Phase 1: Quick Language Detection (First 15 seconds)
- WebSocket to Deepgram with whisper-v3-turbo (fast, multilingual)
- Request first 15 seconds only
- Wait for first transcription chunk
- Use Lingua to detect language from text
- Close WebSocket connection

Phase 2: Full Transcription with Optimal Model
- If Hebrew detected → New WebSocket with ivrit-ct2 model
- If non-Hebrew detected → New WebSocket with deepgram model
- Transcribe full video
- Stream chunks to user in real-time

WEBSOCKET MESSAGE FLOW:
Bot → Deepgram: {url: "...", model: "whisper-v3-turbo", captureMode: "first60"}
Deepgram → Bot: {type: "transcription_chunk", text: "..."}
Bot uses Lingua.DetectLanguage(text) → language
Bot → User: "Detected Hebrew, using ivrit-ct2 for optimal quality..."
Bot → Deepgram: {url: "...", model: "ivrit-ct2", captureMode: "full"}
Deepgram → Bot: Multiple transcription chunks
Bot → User: Stream chunks in real-time

ALTERNATIVE (Simpler but less optimal):
Use whisper-v3-turbo for everything (good for all languages)
Detect language from first chunk
Inform user of detected language
No model switching

User Requirements for /transcribe Command UX Enhancement:

1. **Fetch video metadata FIRST** - Use POST /api/video-info to get:
   - Video title
   - Video duration (formatted as "12min and 13 seconds")
   - Before starting transcription

2. **Verbose progress message** - Show user:
   "Transcribing now "[Video Title]" length: [duration] and Video Language detected: [language]"

3. **NO streaming chunks** - Don't show partial transcription text
   - Only show download progress (percentage)
   - Don't show partial transcription chunks

4. **Final transcription only** - Present complete transcription when done
   - Show full text only when transcription is complete
   - No incremental updates of text

5. **Better expectations** - User knows what to expect:
   - Video title (what they're transcribing)
   - Duration (how long the transcription will take)
   - Language (which model will be used)

API to use: POST http://localhost:8009/api/video-info
Returns: {success: true, data: {title, duration_seconds, duration_formatted, ...}}
